terms.gloss: a meat rack or larder (not a meat tray)
terms.comment: Traupman gives carnārium for a meat tray; classically it is “a frame furnished with hooks to hang up meats over the hearth for smoking”, or a larder (Lewis & Short). A dish for meat is a lānx.

sources: Lewis & Short: lanx
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency: p. 123, checked against the searchable text of the book on 29 October 2026; p. 72.
